title: Who can join the club, and dues
summary: Members are vouched for or investigated; dues are a dollar ten a month, with two meetings a month.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Who can be a member of your club, by the way? Who can join your club?
Well, we just, I mean, I got a good character and he's all right. I'm not a bad fella. There's always somebody vouch for him, you know.
But you have to pass on him somehow, I mean, a membership.

Well, yes, yes they do. They have to pass the decision. If they don't know him, they investigate him. And if they know him, a lot of fellas that we have in our club, the most of them is right around our neighborhood. We know them all. And they in and out. We don't have them. Only time we get strange fellas is like, like this time of year when we're gonna parade. We get fellas from Weaver Industries Canal, anywhere, called them. We know they in there that's what we're gonna parade. Yeah. Yeah, we know that.
Well, how do they pay their dues?

Well, they come up on Sunday. Every month? Every month, yeah, once a month. You see we have two meetings a month. We have the first and the fourth Sunday. And the two later have the second and the fourth Sunday.
You can't make them all. It looks like all those clubs, if they all meet at the same time.

Well, you don't have to go to meet. If you go to meet this Sunday, well you don't have to go, if you make the two land the first Sunday, you don't have to make them no more until the next month. But you make the Jolly Boys the last Sunday. Well most of the fellas that sends their money in, they don't come to meet. They send it in there. Now my secretary has a list stacked that high with the people's name. It'd be right around the corner. And if they won't come to meet, they give me the dollar. They send me a dollar and ten cents a month. They send that dollar and ten cents. And then if I know a fella and he wants to join the club, I mean he's in the club and he's all right, well I'll pay for him. So and so and so. Well we don't, well you see you can't be with two months in the rear. Well all you want, the next month out you go unless somebody pay for you. Well I pay a lot of them fellas that don't get my money back though. Now my wife have a cousin around there, he belongs to Jolly Boy. He don't want a club but he owe me. He don't want a club nothing. He come there, come here a couple of Sundays ago. He says he paid his tax and he paid his due. But he owe me a treat all of them dude. He said he didn't pay me. He said well I'm going to straighten you out. I said okay, all right, go. Pay me as well you know. Pay me as well. Now we got a little fella wait for the checker cab company. See we have a dance, each member is tight for two tickets. Well this little fella got two tickets and he didn't pay and he got out. Now he wants to come back. Now he sent his fees but he didn't send him tickets, that ticket money they turned him down. So I kept his fees there for a whole month. Two months. Eventually he sent the dollar and a half, paid for his two tickets. They took him back in the club. But he's just in there for the parade. After the parade he can get out again.
